title: Global monodromy criterion and conditional symmetry uniqueness for generalized Maurer-Cartan primitives into a homogeneous space
author: Anthony D. Blaom
work: A Characterisation of Smooth Maps into a Homogeneous Space
source_version: Official SIGMA 18 (2022) article 029, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2022.029; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-09-30, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
difficulty_reason: The proof links injective isotropy data to discreteness of Lie-algebroid monodromy and constructs the global primitive through the integrating source-simply-connected groupoid. Its uniqueness argument compares integrated logarithmic derivatives, controls normalizers of the connected isotropy through a principal-bundle homotopy sequence, and passes through the universal covering of the base. This handles global isotropy and symmetry ambiguity beyond the ordinary local Cartan integration theorem.

source_check.note: Full main Theorem3.14 with the existence1.5, integrability Proposition1.3 and complete uniqueness Theorem3.9 proofs is supplied. The base Sigma is connected; omega:A->g satisfies M1 transitivity, M2 isotropy injectivity at a point and M3 isotropy inclusion into an action stabilizer. Existence requires the pointed monodromy to be constant. Uniqueness up to the author Definition3.1 homogeneous-space symmetries additionally requires maximal rank and weakly connected isotropy, meaning equality of the two normalizers N_G(H)=N_G(H^0), not ordinary connected stabilizers. Lie I/II and the established Crainic-Fernandes integrability criterion are background; the new global construction and normalizer comparison are shown. Preserve the source local notation slips in1.8 and the concluding3.12 proof literally, with the warning below; the preceding construction and Proposition3.12 statement explicitly specify the relevant maps, so no new argument is supplied.
